note: Remains of the Vijayanagara empire are found at Hampi: NCERT Theme 7 — the city was sacked in 1565 and deserted, remembered as Hampi, a name derived from the local mother goddess Pampadevi (claim c02); rediscovery by Mackenzie 1800 (c03). Taught in s4 and its did_you_know box.

Ashtadiggajas (the eight Telugu court poets of Krishnadevaraya): named in neither NCERT Class XII Theme 7 nor IGNOU Unit 14, the two sources fetched for this chapter. Source gap — disclosed in the s2 exam_note box; the chapter teaches Krishnadevaraya and the Amuktamalyada (c11) but not the Ashtadiggajas.

Nayankara system: taught in s3 — nayakas/amara-nayakas, their twofold duties (IGNOU Unit 14, c45), amaram tenure (c46), and Venkatramanayya's view that Nayankara is an example of Kakatiya influence (c44).
Amuktamalyada author = Krishnadeva Raya (NCERT Theme 7, c11: 'composed a work on statecraft in Telugu known as the Amuktamalyada'). Taught in s2; practice q04/q38.

Chand Bibi of Ahmednagar: Chand Bibi is named in neither NCERT Theme 7 nor IGNOU Unit 14 fetched for this chapter, and the five Bahmani successor states are not listed there either. Source gap — disclosed in the s5 exam_note box. Partial context taught: Ahmadnagar appears in s6 as one of the three Deccan Sultanates allied at Talikota in 1565 (c15), but that alone does not answer the Chand Bibi question. Primary home would be a Deccan-sultanates treatment (cf. HIS-13 Mughal-era Deccan).
Amuktamalyada author = Krishnadeva Raya (NCERT Theme 7, c11). Same item as WBCS 2021 Q56; taught in s2.
